newsitem.title: FRANCE: Price cut could bring Dassault jet order - DGA.
newsitem.headline: Price cut could bring Dassault jet order - DGA.

text.p: France's DGA arms procurement agency could order 48 of Dassault Aviation's Rafale multi-role combat jets if the plane's makers agree to at least a 10 percent price cut, the agency's head said in a newspaper interview published on Monday.

Jean-Yves Helmer said some of the plane's contractors had already cut their prices by 10 percent and if Dassault and other suppliers followed suit, he could place an order for 48 of the jets. One jet costs about 300 million francs ($57.5 million).
"If we obtain from the builder and its suppliers a cut of at least 10 percent in the Rafale, the DGA could place orders which would concern 48 planes," Helmer told financial daily Les Echos.
"That target remains to be finalised with Dassault Aviation itself and other suppliers," he said.
